plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds erupt into slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue blossoms that hum with bees. Whole hillsides ripple in purple waves, and the scent drifts on warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere, usually peaking in early to mid July
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of Europe
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rose-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Sturdy stems hold them above prairie grasses, and butterflies and goldfinches visit them all summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn, with flowering well underway by late June
plants.location: Prairies and open woodlands of the central and eastern United States
plants.funFact: The central cone is a dense head of many tiny individual flowers. Its spiky look gave the genus a name from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a crown. Silky pink bracts surround a velvety center, and the whole bloom can grow as wide as a dinner plate.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mostly late winter to early summer in South Africa, with a main flush in the austral spring. Some flowering in June, the Southern Hemisphere's winter, is typical.
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. It has evolved to survive the periodic wildfires of the fynbos, resprouting from a woody underground rootstock.
